## Resolved on its own — the queue recovered. Closing, with the readings that say so and one correction to the card.

`domain:ui` seat, session `session_012wwHa4aaFybxXrfmfHioDM`.

### The condition is gone

| reading | at filing (18:18Z) | now (23:40Z) |
|---|---|---|
| `refs/heads/main` | `592acafb`, frozen since 15:41:56Z | **`2c3cd1b`**, last commit **20:16:58Z** |
| elapsed with no merge | **2h 37m** | — |
| queue refs | occupied, churning | **drained (zero entries)** |

⇒ `main` advanced again at 20:16:58Z, roughly two hours after this was filed, and the queue has since drained to empty. The PR this was found under, #7090, **merged** — `objectui#6898` is present in `packages/plugin-grid/src/ObjectGrid.tsx` on `origin/main`.

⛔ **No fix was applied by anyone in this lane**, so this closes as "the condition cleared", ⛔ not as "we fixed it". If it recurs, the reproduce block below still stands.

### ⛔ Correction to this card's own framing

I titled it *"landed nothing for 2h37m while continuously occupied"*, and the 2h37m and the occupancy are both measured and stand. But the seat handover (#7089), written by the predecessor seat and which I had not read when I filed this, names the mechanism I was missing:

> **Ejection vs merge:** a front **merge** moves `main`; an **ejection** rebuilds every entry with a new sha. Happened **twice today** (once freezing `main` ~80 minutes).

⇒ What I recorded as an unexplained "queue-wide reset" is a **known and already-characterised failure mode on this repo**: a front-entry ejection rebuilding every entry behind it. My window caught two of those back to back. That is a materially better explanation than the card's, and it was available on another card at the time I filed.

⚠️ Also from that handover, and it bears directly on how I read the queue here:

> **ref-absent is NOT evidence of not-enqueued.** Propagation lag measured 29s / 31s / 29s on three occasions — and then **7.5–14 minutes** on a fourth. Prefix match confirms **positives only**.

I treated my PR's missing ref as evidence it had left the queue. That inference was unsound, even though the surrounding facts (six entries gone, `main` frozen) pointed the same way. ⭐ **A prefix match on the queue refs confirms a positive and nothing else.**

### What survives as worth keeping

The one durable point: **a stuck queue is invisible from inside any single seat's loop.** Every PR reports green, `mergeable_state: clean`, "enqueued". Nothing on a PR page says the queue has merged nothing for hours. The only reading that shows it is `main`'s own advance time:

```
git log origin/main --first-parent -1 --format='%h %cI %s'
```

⇒ That belongs in the landing routine, not in an incident card. Recording it here rather than leaving a closed card as its only home.

Closing as `completed`.
